name: OpenAI
description: Creator of the GPT-4.1 API family and the GPT-5 line (GPT-5, GPT-5.4, GPT-5.5, and the current GPT-5.6 family of Sol, Terra, and Luna).

name: Anthropic
description: Creator of the Claude models, offered only as a hosted service through the Claude API and partner clouds.

name: Google DeepMind
description: The Google research team that builds the Gemini models, formed by combining Google Brain and DeepMind.

name: Meta
description: Creator of the Llama models, published as downloadable weights under Meta's own community licences.

name: SpaceXAI
description: The creator of the Grok models, served through a hosted API with no downloadable weights. Its own surfaces do not agree on one name: x.ai titles its news pages "SpaceXAI" and carries the footer "© 2026 SpaceXAI LLC", while the developer documentation on docs.x.ai describes the same models as "SpaceXAI’s frontier model" and the interface as "the xAI API". Both names are first-party and nothing checked on either site states a rename, so both are recorded and neither is asserted to have replaced the other.

name: Mistral AI
description: A French creator that publishes downloadable weights on its verified Hugging Face organization alongside a hosted API, and that uses more than one licence across the models it publishes. Its Hugging Face display name is written "Mistral AI_"; the trailing underscore is treated as a display artefact rather than part of the name.

name: DeepSeek
description: A Chinese creator that publishes open weights under the MIT licence. Both www.deepseek.com and api-docs.deepseek.com failed at the transport layer when checked on 2026-08-28, on two independent attempts each, so no page on the creator’s own domain could be read. The website and release page recorded here are its verified Hugging Face organization, which is the first-party surface that could be reached, and every DeepSeek fact in this dataset is read from there rather than from the creator’s own domain.

name: Alibaba Cloud
description: The creator of the Qwen model family. The Qwen team’s own Hugging Face organization states that Qwen "refers to the large language model family built by Alibaba Cloud", and this dataset records Alibaba Cloud as the creator on that basis. The team does not write the attribution identically everywhere: the QwenLM/Qwen3.8 repository credits "Qwen team, Alibaba Group", the parent company, while the Hugging Face profile credits Alibaba Cloud. That conflict is recorded rather than resolved. Qwen models are offered by clouds Alibaba Cloud does not operate, including Amazon SageMaker JumpStart; being served somewhere is never evidence of who built the model.

name: Microsoft
description: A company that occupies three roles this dataset keeps apart. It creates model families, through Microsoft AI, which builds the MAI line, and through Microsoft Research, which publishes the Fara line; those are the only Microsoft records treated as models. It ships Microsoft Copilot, which is a product and is recorded as one. It operates Microsoft Foundry, which is a serving platform and is recorded as one. A model appearing in Microsoft Foundry is a deployment fact and never evidence that Microsoft created it.

name: Amazon
description: The creator of the Amazon Nova model family, which AWS states is "built on AI technologies originally developed for Amazon’s internal applications". Amazon also operates Amazon Bedrock and Amazon SageMaker JumpStart, which serve models created by other organizations — Bedrock’s own page offers "hundreds of FMs from leading AI companies" — and this dataset records those as serving platforms, never as evidence of authorship. Amazon’s announcements are published by Amazon Web Services, whose wording alternates between naming Amazon and naming AWS as the announcing entity.

name: Cohere
description: The creator of the Command models, which its own model cards attribute to "Cohere Inc.". Cohere reaches customers through its hosted API, where it separates free "trial" keys from billed "production" usage, and publishes some models as downloadable weights as well. Cohere Labs is Cohere's research arm and the voice behind the separate Aya line; the clouds that resell Command models are serving platforms, not co-creators.

name: Allen Institute for AI
description: A Seattle-based nonprofit research institute whose OLMo project releases fully open language models, publishing weights, training data, and code.

name: Technology Innovation Institute
description: An Abu Dhabi government research institute whose AI unit develops the open-weight Falcon family of language models.

name: NVIDIA
description: A US technology company whose research teams publish the open-weight Nemotron model family. Its separate hardware and inference-platform roles are not recorded here as creator facts.

name: AI21 Labs
description: An Israeli AI company that builds the Jamba family of hybrid SSM-Transformer models, released as open weights and offered through its paid API.

name: Zhipu AI
description: A Chinese AI company, originating from Tsinghua University research, that develops the open-weight GLM model family and offers paid API access.

name: Moonshot AI
description: A Chinese AI company that develops the Kimi model family, released as open weights and served through its paid API.

name: EleutherAI
description: A non-profit research lab that states its focus as the interpretability, alignment, and ethics of artificial intelligence, and publishes its open models on Hugging Face. It develops the Pythia suite and the GPT-NeoX training library.

name: LG AI Research
description: The research organization that develops and releases the EXAONE family of instruction-tuned bilingual English and Korean language models, published under its own LGAI-EXAONE namespace.

name: Snowflake
description: The company whose Snowflake AI Research team pre-trained the Arctic dense-MoE hybrid language models from scratch and published the weights under Apache-2.0.

name: Upstage
description: The company that develops the Solar language models, built with a depth up-scaling method that extends a smaller model into a larger one.
